non_claims: This inspection records WHICH owners were read, not at what content, and not that any of them is correct, complete, or repaired. Content is deliberately unpinned (#562).
No product behavior of cmanki or craken-agents is claimed; those repos are read-only comparison evidence.
Listing a locator under an issue does not assert that issue's fix lives there; it asserts the surface was inspected while scoping that issue.

HISTORICAL, and no longer enforced. The figures, stated once so they stop reading as a contradiction: 6 of 20 locators had their content change over roughly one day, and the inspection was re-stamped 5 times across 4 distinct locators (one of them twice). The 2026-08-08 re-stamps were an operator POLICY ruling, not a re-inspection, and the scope conclusions built on those locators were not re-derived. #562 then retired the digest pin entirely, so nothing here asserts any locator's content is current. A locator whose semantics actually change still needs a real re-read, and no gate will now tell you when that happened.
purpose: Record which producer/consumer surfaces were actually read before the #514/#515/#518 acceptance matrix was built. Each locator's path must still resolve to a real file, and the inspection identity binds the locator SET, so a surface cannot be added, dropped, or re-roled without the freeze failing. It does NOT bind file CONTENT: #562 retired the per-locator digest pin after measuring 0 true positives in 5 refusals, so an edit to an inspected file is no longer a refusal and this record does not assert that any inspected surface is unchanged since it was read.
